title: Unfortunate News for AMD Stock Investors
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; note: captions garble some names and figures in places
summary: Parkevtate covers AMD's ~9–10% Thursday drop after Hunterbrook Media alleged the chipmaker skirted export controls by continuing to supply firmware updates to blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT, with three associated companies allegedly using near-identical firmware. He stresses Hunterbrook Capital holds a short position in AMD, so he discounts short-seller claims, and notes AMD denies the allegations, saying it complies with US export controls. Still, he says the dip is not a buying opportunity: AMD is overvalued at a forward P/E of 30 versus Nvidia's 10, and his DCF fair value is $390 against a ~$479 market price, roughly 20% above intrinsic value. He recalls ranking AMD a buying opportunity in earlier years and downgrading it after the share price soared, most recently on 3 November. AMD's revenue and EPS growth could rival Nvidia's as it catches up in data centres, but a triple valuation premium makes no sense to him. He leans toward believing AMD over the short seller but prefers Nvidia at current valuations. Call: AMD AVOID at ~$479 (FV $390) — a flip from HOLD (15 Nov); NVDA BUY reiterated.
